expects.query: Check if the warehouse_safety_0001 video is already uploaded on VST. If it doesn't exist, upload the warehouse_safety_0001 video to VIOS with timestamp 2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z. If it exists, skip the uploading.
checks: Trajectory shows the agent verified `warehouse_safety_0001` exists in VST at some point during the trial — e.g. listing sensors/streams via the agent tools or a REST call to `/vst/api/v1/sensor/list`. The probe order relative to any upload step is not enforced; what matters is that the agent confirmed presence before any `/generate` (report) call.
curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list returns a JSON array containing a sensor whose name matches the uploaded video's filename stem

curl -sf http://localhost:${VSS_PUBLIC_PORT:-7777}/vst/api/v1/sensor/<sensorId>/streams returns a non-empty streams array whose main stream's url is a local file path under /home/vst/... or similar (NOT rtsp://). The /vst/* path goes through the HAProxy ingress (port 7777 by default); the direct VST port 30888 may not be host-bound on all deploys, so prefer the public/HAProxy port for the verifier-side curl.

expects.query: Verify the VSS stack is ready for the **report** skill. Confirm VST reachable and at least one stream is registered, the VLM endpoint resolves, and a clip can actually be materialized for warehouse_safety_0001. IMPORTANT: warehouse_safety_0001 is the sensor NAME, not its streamId — a VIOS file upload assigns a random UUID as sensorId/streamId. First resolve the real streamId: GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list and take the sensorId/streamId of the entry whose name is warehouse_safety_0001 (it will be a UUID, e.g. 1a2d7922-...). Then fetch the recorded timeline via GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/<streamId>/timelines and request a short (2-3s) clip URL for a range INSIDE that timeline (the video was uploaded at timestamp 2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, so a range like startTime=2025-01-01T00:00:01.000Z&endTime=2025-01-01T00:00:03.000Z is safe) using GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>/url with container=mp4&disableAudio=true. Report any HTTP 500 from the clip endpoint as a blocker rather than proceeding.
checks: curl -sf --max-time 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version returns 200
curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/streams returns HTTP 200 and a non-empty JSON body

The run resolved the streamId for the warehouse_safety_0001 sensor (via GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/list or /sensor/streams, matching name=warehouse_safety_0001 to its sensorId/streamId — which is a UUID for VIOS file uploads, NOT the literal filename) and then fetched the recorded timeline (GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/<streamId>/timelines using that resolved streamId) returning a non-empty {startTime, endTime} range anchored near 2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, BEFORE constructing any clip URL, rather than guessing clip times. Using the sensor NAME in the storage path (which 404s) instead of the resolved UUID streamId is a failure.

The run performed a successful GET to the VST clip-URL endpoint http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>/url — where <streamId> is the resolved sensorId/streamId (UUID) for warehouse_safety_0001, NOT the literal sensor name — with startTime and endTime query params inside the recorded timeline plus container=mp4 and disableAudio=true, and received HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing a non-empty videoUrl (confirms clip materialization works; a 500 here is a blocker for the report step, but a 404 solely from using the sensor name instead of the resolved streamId does not count as success).

Either VLM_BASE_URL + VLM_NAME (NIM Cosmos) or RTVI_VLM_BASE_URL/RTVI_VLM_ENDPOINT + RTVI_VLM_MODEL_TO_USE (RT-VLM Cosmos) are resolvable from the vss-agent container environment (e.g. docker exec vss-agent env returns one set), and a GET against the chosen endpoint's /v1/models returns 200 with the model id present in .data[].id

expects.query:
Give me a report for warehouse_safety_0001. VSS agent is on http://localhost:8000

**Environment & prerequisites:** Use Mode A path A1 (VST clip URL) — the video is already uploaded to VST. warehouse_safety_0001 is the sensor NAME; resolve its real streamId first (GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list, match name=warehouse_safety_0001 to its sensorId/streamId, which is a UUID for VIOS file uploads — using the name in the storage path 404s). Before requesting a clip, fetch the recorded timeline (GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/<streamId>/timelines) and pick a short (2-3s) range INSIDE it; the upload timestamp is 2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z so a range like startTime=2025-01-01T00:00:01.000Z&endTime=2025-01-01T00:00:03.000Z is safe. Always pass container=mp4&disableAudio=true on the clip request (GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>/url). Do NOT fall back to the A2 local-file/base64 path while VST is reachable and serving this sensor; if the clip endpoint returns HTTP 500, retry with a timeline-correct range rather than switching to base64.
checks: The run sourced the clip via the Mode A path A1 (VST clip URL) rather than an A2 base64 data URL or POST /generate. It is sufficient that the run obtained a clip URL of the form http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>/url with startTime/endTime query params plus container=mp4&disableAudio=true and a JSON body containing videoUrl — this MAY reuse a clip URL already materialized in the readiness step (step 3) and does not require a second successful GET here. A transient VST 500 on a re-fetch does not fail this check as long as a valid A1 clip URL was obtained (this step or the prior readiness step) and used as the VLM video_url.

The run performed at least one successful POST to /v1/chat/completions on the resolved VLM endpoint (either ${VLM_BASE_URL}/v1 for NIM Cosmos or ${RTVI_VLM_BASE_URL}/v1 / ${RTVI_VLM_ENDPOINT} for RT-VLM Cosmos), with Content-Type application/json, a JSON body containing model matching whatever the resolved endpoint's /v1/models advertises for this deployment (base-profile default is nvidia/cosmos3-nano-reasoner; other valid NIM ids include nvidia/cosmos3-super-reasoner, nvidia/cosmos-reason2-8b, nvidia/cosmos-reason1-7b, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct; RT-VLM uses cosmos-reason2 / openai-compat matching RTVI_VLM_MODEL_TO_USE), and a messages array whose first user content list contains both a text block and a video_url block referencing the clip URL from the prior step; HTTP 2xx.
The run did NOT POST to http://localhost:8000/generate.
The user-facing markdown has a single top-level title line matching # Video Analysis Report (allows leading whitespace after #).

The markdown contains ## Basic Information followed by a pipe-table (Field | Value) including every row header from the skill template: Report Identifier; Date of Analysis; Time of Analysis; Video Source; Clip Range, Clip URL; VLM; Analysis Request — each paired cell is filled with concrete text (no raw placeholders like literal <sensor_id>, <YYYY-MM-DD>, '<e.g.', or duplicate Field names without values).
The Basic Information Report Identifier row value matches pattern vss_report_ followed by 8-digit date (YYYYMMDD), underscore, and 6-digit time (HHMMSS) as in SKILL (vss_report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>).
The Basic Information Date of Analysis value looks like calendar date YYYY-MM-DD (four digits-two digits-two digits) not a template stub; Time of Analysis looks like HH:MM:SS.
The Basic Information Video Source row names warehouse_safety_0001

The Basic Information VLM row names the model actually returned by the chat/completions call for this deployment (e.g. nvidia/cosmos3-nano-reasoner or nvidia/cosmos3-super-reasoner for the base NIM Cosmos default, nvidia/cosmos-reason2-8b, or the RT-VLM model id from RTVI_VLM_MODEL_TO_USE) rather than a placeholder; match the live model id, do not require one specific name.
The Basic Information Analysis Request row restates or paraphrases the user ask (report about warehouse_safety_0001 context) rather than staying empty.

The markdown contains ## Analysis Results and beneath it substantive content: the VLM caption summary with timestamps or time segments (seconds or ranges), chronological sense, non-empty—not only headings or placeholders. Any <think>...</think> reasoning block from Cosmos Reason VLMs is stripped before insertion.
The Analysis Results content is visibly derived from the VLM response (caption-style description); it is not a single sentence like N/A covering the whole section unless the VLM truly returned that.

The run inserted exactly one synthetic incident document into Elasticsearch index mdx-vlm-incidents, not just mdx-incidents.
The inserted document contained at least these fields: Id, id, timestamp, end, sensorId, category, type, objectIds, info.verdict.
The run initialized a VA-MCP session against http://localhost:9901/mcp with a POST method=initialize and extracted mcp-session-id from the response header.

The run did NOT redeploy alerts profile and did NOT insert only into mdx-incidents

expects.query: Give me a report on the last incident.
checks: The run initialized a VA-MCP session against http://localhost:9901/mcp (POST with method=initialize) and extracted mcp-session-id from the response header.

The run issued at least one tools/call POST to http://localhost:9901/mcp with the mcp-session-id header set, calling video_analytics__get_incidents with max_count=1, or calling video_analytics__get_incident if an incident ID was already known.
The run did NOT POST to http://localhost:8000/generate and did NOT POST to a VLM chat/completions endpoint for this incident-range query (Mode B routes through analytics, not VLM).

If a report was generated, the markdown ## Basic Information table contains rows Report Identifier, Range, Scope, Total Incidents, Confirmed / Rejected / Unverified — each filled with concrete values consistent with the VA-MCP response.
